title: Egypt Tour Deposits & Cancellation Terms: What to Check
excerpt: Egypt tour deposits and cancellation terms explained: what to check before you pay, and how Sawa takes a deposit only once a date confirms (10% on day tours, 25% on packages).
body_html:
Prices, timetables and visiting details are a November 2026 snapshot. Check the linked official pages and your departure’s current inclusions and terms before booking.

Quick answer

The size of an Egypt tour deposit matters less than when it is charged and what the cancellation terms do to it. A small deposit taken at booking can cost you more than a larger one taken after the trip is confirmed. On Sawa Tours, reserving is free and nothing is charged before a date confirms with four travellers (the GoAhead). On a day tour you then pay a 10% deposit, and the balance is due 2 days before departure. Cancel at least 48 hours before departure and you get a full refund, deposit included. Cancel inside 48 hours and you lose the 10% deposit. Packages and cruises work on longer timings: a 25% deposit, the balance 14 days before, and a cancellation scale that starts 30 days out.

MoneyHelper explains how Section 75 and chargeback work, including their conditions and limits.

Key facts

Fact Detail
What a deposit is The part you pay to hold a place before travel. The rest (the balance) follows on a stated date
When Sawa charges Only once a date confirms at four travellers (the GoAhead). Reserving a seat is free and nothing is charged before that
Deposit Day tours: 10% of the price, by payment link at the GoAhead. Packages and cruises: 25%
Balance Day tours: due 2 days (48 hours) before departure. Packages and cruises: 14 days before
If the date never reaches four A day-tour date has until 7 days before the tour, a package date until 30 days before. If it does not get there it is cancelled, nothing was charged, and another date is suggested
Day tours: cancelling at least 48 hours before departure Full refund, deposit included
Day tours: cancelling less than 48 hours before departure Deposit retained (10% of the tour price)
Packages and cruises: cancelling 30+ days before: no charge. 29 to 15 days: half the deposit (12.5%). 14 days or fewer, or no-show: the deposit (25%) is kept
Force majeure (riots, revolution and similar) Full refund
Missing a payment A traveller who does not pay after the GoAhead is excluded from the tour. The tour keeps running for everyone else
Confirmed dates Not cancelled for low numbers

Every deposit is a bet on timing

Every Egypt booking reaches the same awkward moment: someone asks for money before anything is certain. The deposit stage is where travellers get burned. It is not usually because operators are dishonest. It is because the terms doing all the work are five clauses long and nobody reads them until something goes wrong. This guide teaches you to read those five clauses, gives you twelve questions to ask before paying, and uses Sawa's own terms as the worked example. We are the people behind Sawa Tours (sawa.tours), the Egypt shared-departure platform. We have worked in Egyptian tourism since 1993, first as a guide and then running an agency, and we publish our payment terms openly so that you can run this test on them, and on anyone else's.

Deposit sizes for Egypt tours: what is normal

Deposit sizes vary widely between operators and between trip types. Some day tours ask for nothing until the day, while multi-day packages and cruise-heavy itineraries commonly ask for a much larger share because hotels and cabins are committed early. The number alone tells you little. Balance windows follow the same logic: a day tour can be paid for days before departure, while a package may need the balance weeks out.

Here is the sentence to carry with you: the deposit's size matters less than when it is charged and what the cancellation terms do to it. A 10% deposit taken at booking, months before anyone knows the departure will run, can be worse than a 25% deposit taken after confirmation. The timing is the protection.

In real money: the Aswan to Abu Simbel day tour is from €50 per person, as listed in November 2026. Once its date confirms at four travellers, the 10% deposit is €5. The balance of €45 is due 2 days before departure. Cancel at least 48 hours before departure and both come back in full.

On a package the same logic runs on a longer clock. Egypt in Depth, nine days with a Nile cruise, is from €1,403 per person, as listed in November 2026. The 25% deposit at the GoAhead is €350.75, and the balance of €1,052.25 is due 14 days before departure.

The five clauses that decide whether you get money back

Every operator's small print runs on the same five clauses. Each one below shows how Sawa handles it, what it means in practice, and the trap version to watch for.

1. Deposit and balance due date

On a Sawa day tour, the 10% deposit is due by payment link as soon as the date confirms at four travellers, and the balance is due 2 days before departure. If a date confirms close to departure, the deposit and balance may be collected together. On a package or cruise the deposit is 25% and the balance is due 14 days before. A traveller who does not pay after the GoAhead is excluded, and the tour keeps running for the others. What it means: your money is committed only after the trip is real, and the dates are written down. The trap: deposits charged at booking, months before anyone knows the departure will run, or a balance date that is never stated.

2. Cancellation terms

Before the GoAhead there is nothing to cancel: reserving is free, so you can drop a seat at no cost. After the GoAhead on a day tour, cancelling at least 48 hours before departure is a full refund, including your deposit. Cancelling less than 48 hours before departure means the 10% deposit is retained. On a package or cruise, cancelling 30 or more days before is free, 29 to 15 days before costs half the deposit (12.5% of the price), and 14 days or fewer, or a no-show, means the 25% deposit is kept. Some package components, such as flights, cabins or permits, may become non-refundable earlier; this is disclosed before you pay. What it means: clear lines with dates attached. You know exactly when each window closes. The trap: tiers expressed as percentages of the full price that start climbing weeks or months out, so that your money is partly lost long before the trip. Ask for the tiers as a short table of dates and amounts.

3. The minimum numbers clause

On Sawa the minimum is four travellers (people, not bookings, so a party of four can confirm a date alone). A day-tour date has until 7 days before the tour to reach four, and a package date until 30 days before. Miss that and the date is cancelled, with nothing charged, and another date is suggested. Once a date is confirmed, it is not cancelled for low numbers. What it means: the low-numbers risk sits with the platform, not with you. The trap: "the operator may substitute a similar tour or issue a credit" instead of refunding. Our post on why Egypt group tours get cancelled unpacks this clause in depth.

4. Force majeure

Force majeure is the clause for events beyond anyone's control. Read how the operator defines it and, above all, what happens to your money when it applies. On Sawa, in a force majeure event such as riots or a revolution, you receive a full refund. What it means: a genuine no-fault event does not cost you your payment. The trap: force majeure written as a blank-cheque exit with no refund duty at all, or one that pays you back only in credit.

5. Refund timeline and method

Ask for a countable promise: a number of days, to the payment method you used. What it means: you can hold the operator to a date. The trap: "within a reasonable time", or refunds issued as vouchers at the operator's discretion. Sawa's terms say refunds are made within 14 business days. Whatever an operator says, get the refund period in writing before you pay.

Cancellation runs both ways: when they cancel and when you do

The same small print is two contracts, and you should read both. You cancelling triggers the cancellation terms in clause 2. The operator cancelling is the other contract. On Sawa, the main way that happens is a forming date that does not reach four travellers by its deadline (7 days before a day tour, 30 days before a package): it is cancelled and nothing was charged, so there is nothing to refund. A confirmed date is not cancelled for low numbers. A traveller who misses a payment is excluded without ending the trip for the others.

Two checks follow. First, the asymmetry check: never accept terms where their cancellation still burns your deposit. Second, the material-change check: a major change, such as a different destination, duration or accommodation standard, should give you the same accept-an-alternative-or-cancel choice, while minor timing or guide changes do not count. And one lesson the whole industry learned the hard way: a credit note is a bet on the operator's survival. Insist on cash, or on written credit terms with an expiry you can live with. For the wider pattern, see why Egypt group tours get cancelled.

Common mistakes when paying an Egypt tour deposit

  • Paying by bank transfer to a personal account instead of by card, which loses the chargeback fallback.
  • Booking non-refundable international flights before the departure date is confirmed.
  • Missing the balance-due date. Some terms treat it as a cancellation with the deposit forfeit, and on Sawa a missed payment means exclusion from the tour.
  • Assuming "confirmed" means unconditional. A confirmed departure still runs under the cancellation and force majeure clauses.
  • Not screenshotting the terms on booking day. Pages change, and the version you agreed to is the one that counts.

Your protections when paying an Egypt operator

Protections come in layers, not absolutes. Ministry of Tourism licensing and ETAA registration are the floor: they tell you the company is real and accountable, but they are not in themselves a refund promise. Package travel rules, such as the EU Package Travel Directive and the UK regime, protect some packages sold in those markets. Whether they cover a particular booking depends on how the trip is sold and by whom, so ask. Paying by card gives you the chargeback fallback: card disputes are commonly allowed for about 120 days from the transaction, and sometimes longer where the service has not yet been delivered, though your own card issuer's rules decide. Travel insurance fills the gaps that no terms can: medical treatment, evacuation, and the cost of a cancelled trip outside the refund window. Sawa's terms require cover for medical treatment, evacuation and repatriation, and recommend cancellation cover.

If something does go wrong, the complaint path matters as much as the terms. Ask in advance who you contact, how, and how quickly they must reply. On Sawa, write to hello@sawa.tours, or use WhatsApp while your tour is running.

The 12-question pre-booking checklist

Run this checklist on any operator's terms before money moves. Each question carries the shape of a good answer.

Before you pay:

  1. How much is the deposit, and what triggers it? A specific percentage tied to confirmation, not to your enquiry.
  2. When is the balance due, and what happens if I miss it? A stated date, with the miss rule written down.
  3. What can make the price change after booking? A closed list (taxes, legal changes), not "at our discretion".
  4. What exactly is in writing? An invoice naming the tour, dates, operator and price.

Cancellation and refunds:

  1. What are the cancellation tiers and their deadlines? A short table of dates and amounts.
  2. Is there a minimum-numbers clause? A stated minimum and deadline, with a full refund if it is missed.
  3. If the operator cancels, what do I get? A refund or an equivalent alternative, not a credit "at our discretion".
  4. What does force majeure cover, and how are refunds calculated? A defined list and a clear refund rule.
  5. How long do refunds take, and to where? A day count, to the original payment method.

If things go wrong:

  1. How do I complain, and what are the response deadlines? A named contact and a day count for each step.
  2. What are my fallbacks, such as the chargeback window and insurance cover? Card payment encouraged, insurance requirements stated.
  3. Which law governs the contract, and which of my home rights survive? A named law, with mandatory home-country rights preserved.

Practical tips before you hand over money

  • The invoice is the promise. Tour name, dates, operating company and total price, in writing, before any payment.
  • Screenshot the terms on booking day. Terms pages get updated, and the version you agreed to is the one that counts.
  • Pay by card, never by transfer to a personal account. The chargeback right exists on card payments, not on transfers.
  • Ask the GoAhead-style question: "What minimum triggers this trip, and by when?" If the answer is vague, the cancellation risk is yours.
  • Check what a retained deposit actually covers. On some operators' terms it can be the whole price.

Red flags and green flags in tour terms

Clause Green flag Red flag
Deposit timing Charged at confirmation, or small and dated Large deposit at booking, months out
Cancellation Clear dates and amounts, with a long free-cancel window Percentages of the full price that reach 100% early
Low numbers Minimum and deadline stated; automatic refund if missed "Similar tour or credit" instead of a refund
Force majeure Defined events; refund duty stated Open-ended escape with no refund duty
Refunds Day count, to the original method "Reasonable time", vouchers at discretion
Changes Material changes trigger accept-or-cancel "We may amend itineraries at any time"

The honest downside, in one place: even the best terms let an operator keep what it has already spent on your behalf, and that is why travel insurance exists for the gap. On a Sawa day tour, the cliff is the 48-hour line: inside it, you lose the 10% deposit. No terms make a cancelled trip cost nothing once the vehicle, the guide and the entrance tickets are booked. Good terms just make sure it costs you the least, and tell you when.

How Sawa handles deposits differently

Sawa Tours (sawa.tours) is an Egypt shared-departure platform. It pools travellers on the same date of a fixed tour, and it reverses the usual payment order. You reserve a seat on a forming date (a date that has not yet reached four travellers) for free, and nothing is charged. When the fourth traveller joins, the date reaches the GoAhead and is confirmed to run. The operating agency is one of the licensed Egyptian agencies with travellers on the date, named before the deposit is due. Only then is the deposit due (10% on a day tour, 25% on a package), paid by a secure payment link from Online Era (General Sales Agent licence 32241); charges are in euros. The platform is operated by Online Era, registration 148500. Prices are fixed per traveller, and day tours have no solo surcharge. The full step-by-step is in how the GoAhead works, the GoAhead promise sets out what Sawa commits to, and how shared departures work covers the model. Questions about a specific date? Message Sawa on WhatsApp at +20 109 284 7613, answered 24/7 while your tour is running.

The short version

Pay late, read the terms, get it in writing. A deposit's size matters less than its timing, and the cancellation terms decide what it can cost you. The five clauses above tell you in five minutes. On Sawa, reserving is free, nothing is charged until a date confirms at four travellers, and the deposit is 10% on a day tour (balance 2 days before) or 25% on a package (balance 14 days before). A good operator's terms survive being read slowly, ours included. Read Sawa's terms and FAQ, reserve free on the forming departures, or message Sawa on WhatsApp at +20 109 284 7613, answered 24/7 while your tour is running.

faq.q: What should I ask before booking an Egypt tour?

faq.q: What happens if my group tour is cancelled for low numbers?

Read what the operator owes you when it applies. On Sawa, a force majeure event such as riots or a revolution means a full refund. A clause with no refund duty at all is a red flag.

faq.q: What happens if I cancel a Sawa tour after paying the deposit?
faq.a: On a day tour: more than 48 hours before departure, you get a full refund, deposit included; less than 48 hours before departure, you lose the 10% deposit. On a package or cruise: 30 or more days before, no charge; 29 to 15 days, half the deposit; 14 days or fewer, the deposit is kept. If you do not pay after the GoAhead, you are excluded from the tour, and it keeps running for everyone else.

faq.q: How long should a refund from an Egypt tour operator take?
faq.a: A countable number of days, not "a reasonable time", paid to the method you used. Ask for the figure in writing before you pay. Sawa's terms say 14 business days. If a stated deadline passes, the card chargeback route is the fallback, which is exactly why paying by card matters.
